roadmap.goal: Slice 01 only: stop one slow Portfolio refresh from starving every Team refresh. The update queue's single Channel becomes three - Team, Portfolio, Forecast - one channel and one reader task each, routed by a total function of UpdateType evaluated at enqueue time, and a queued row is told what is holding its OWN lane rather than whichever running row the store happened to hand back first. Source: ADO User Story #5877, tagged Release Notes, related to Epic #5511; reported from a 26.8.14.1 standalone instance (Tauri, macOS, SQLite, Jira Data Center) where a Portfolio refresh ran 77.7 minutes, failed on DNS, and its coalesced follow-up retook the loop - 3h38m with zero team updates, cleared only by a restart. Backend-dominant: two production classes changed, three small new ones, one read-model line, one frontend comment. No endpoint, no DTO, no EF migration, no config key, no client change. DISTILL has already authored the 12 tests this slice must turn green (8 acceptance scenarios plus the precursor commit's 4), all [Ignore]d; DELIVER implements production code and un-skips them as it goes. The load-bearing ordering is that the precursor commit lands FIRST: the single reader loop is currently the only thing making WriteBackRound safe, and introducing a second reader before the lock exists ships a data race on the write path to a customer's work tracking system.

out_of_scope: Slice 02 in its entirety - the wall-time bound. DESIGN's deferred question 5 and DISCUSS's Prioritization both place slice 02's go/no-go AFTER slice 01 has been dogfooded on a real instance, and both say it may legitimately be dropped rather than deferred: if teams keep moving, a stuck portfolio becomes a slow portfolio rather than a dead instance and the bound changes from a rescue to a tidy-up. Planning it now would be planning for a world slice 01 may have already removed. Step 01-06 is where the answer is written down.

Every slice-02 component named in DESIGN's Component Decomposition: UpdateRunDeadline, IUpdateRunDeadlines, the Update:MaxRunMinutes AppSettings key, IAppSettingService/AppSettingService/AppSettingKeys, AppSettingsController and its two new routes, the RefreshLog reason column and both migration projects, SyncOutcome, TeamUpdater/PortfolioUpdater/ForecastUpdater's refresh-log finally, SystemSettingsTab.tsx, RefreshHistorySection.tsx, SettingsService.ts and RefreshLog.ts

Slice02NothingHoldsALaneForeverScenarios.cs / Slice02NothingHoldsALaneForeverSpecifications.cs - 17 [Ignore]d tests that stay ignored, and the harness members that serve them (GivenTheInstanceRunLimitIsRecordedAs, GivenNoRunLimitHasEverBeenRecorded, TheRecordedRunOf) which stay unused by slice 01. TheRefreshHistory is the exception as of 2026-09-18: step 01-04b reads it to count forecast executions on a production seam.
DISTILL obligation 3 - 'the bound's decision function performs no I/O' (ArchUnitNET). It guards a slice-02 type that does not exist yet; it lands with UpdateRunDeadline.
DISTILL obligation 6 - 'both new app-settings routes carry the guard' (integration test enumerating them). Same reason: the routes are slice 02's.

ThreeLaneSqliteWriteProbe.cs - already runs green and already answered DESIGN's deferred question 1 (yes for safety, no for fairness: nothing is refused, but the incumbent re-takes the write lock and three lanes saving hard do not interleave). No step plans work for it, and nothing in this slice re-probes it or acts on the fairness finding - a write-serialising gate or per-lane save batching is not needed, because nothing holds a write transaction across a connector call.

Per-connection lanes, or a per-connection concurrency limit inside the Portfolio lane. ADR-195 records it as the named cheaper next step and explicitly not scheduled - only if a real instance shows two trackers starving each other.
Priority or preemption between lanes. Lanes are independent, not ranked.
Two refreshes of the same type in parallel (D3). Same-type serialisation is the deliberate half of this change, not the part left undone.
Persisting queue wait in RefreshLog - refused in DESIGN Q5. QueuedAt/StartedAt live in the status store, which ADR-076 defines as a non-authoritative coordination projection.

Any LANE-RELATED change to IUpdateStatusStore or either of its adapters. A lane is a queue-implementation fact and must not enter a port two adapters implement; WaitingBehind is resolved on the read path in the controller, deliberately. NARROWED on 2026-09-18 by ADR-198: step 01-04b adds one scoped liveness predicate - HasActiveWork(keys) - to that port, and the reason above is preserved in full because no lane enters the port. The Reuse Analysis row marking IUpdateStatusStore REUSE AS-IS is superseded for that one member and for nothing else.
Any change to UpdateServiceBase.WriteSummaryIfTheRoundIsOver. Its check-then-act on HasFinished is absorbed by 01-01's atomic take, not fixed at the call site.

The orphaned-feature cleanup finally at PortfolioUpdater.cs:176. It is a potential data-loss path with a different root cause and a different urgency, split to its own Bug by user decision on 2026-09-18, to be raised before #5877 resolves. No step below reaches it and the outer finally at :174-177 is not modified.

Postgres container fixtures for the execution lock or the status store. Both are unchanged by this slice and already exercised by Integration/Containers; adding a fixture here would re-test an unchanged adapter.
Mutation testing (Stryker.NET and frontend Stryker), /nw-finalize, docs prose, release notes, ADO transitions and pushing - the user reviews the delivered slice first

Per-feature screenshots - N/A, because nothing changes what a screenshot would show. The task list's rows already render the same way; only how many can read Running at once differs, and that is not a stable thing to capture. (Slice 02 is where screenshots become due.)
Lighthouse-Clients CLI / MCP version bump - N/A, because no client-facing contract changes (D12). UpdateTaskResponse keeps its shape; only WaitingBehind's meaning is corrected.
RBAC - N/A, because no gate is added, removed or moved (D10). The task list and its cancel route are already System Administrator only.

phases.name: Teams keep moving while a portfolio refresh runs
phases.description: Slice 01. A Platform Operator opens the Task Manager popover while a long Portfolio refresh is running and sees the Team row reading Running beside the Portfolio's, with that Team's dashboard showing a fresh last-updated moment - and a queued row that names what is holding its own lane instead of inventing a dependency. Ordered so that every mechanism the single reader was silently making safe is made safe before the second reader exists.

steps.name: Precursor commit - a write-back round survives two executions at once
criteria: Stage, TakeStaged, ReportRefresh, ReportForecast and TakeSummary all run under one lock owned by the round; Join, Leave and HasFinished keep their Interlocked / Volatile implementations untouched
500 stagings from each of two threads into one round leave 1000 updates for the writer - the union of what both staged, nothing lost and nothing duplicated
TakeStaged is read-and-clear in one step: the first caller receives what the round was holding and a second caller receives an empty set

TakeSummary is read-and-clear in one step: the first caller receives the folded summary and a second receives null, so two executions that both believe the round has finished produce one line and not two
Staging into a round whose staged set has already been handed over throws InvalidOperationException rather than being swallowed
Last stage wins within one execution is preserved exactly: two passes over the same (connection, work item, target field) leave the later value, written once
An ArchUnitNET rule fails the build if anything outside WriteBackRound reads or writes its backing state
A source scanner fails the build if anything other than UpdateQueueService assigns WriteBackRoundContext.Current, mirroring the shape of UpdateCancellationContextWriterArchUnitTest
All four tests in WriteBackRoundConcurrencyTest.cs are un-skipped and green, stable over three consecutive runs
The QuietWriteBack and epic-5511-task-manager categories stay green without being edited; dotnet build zero warnings; the non-connector dotnet test filter green
Committed on its own, before UpdateLanes exists
steps.implementation_notes:
THIS STEP LANDS FIRST AND ON ITS OWN, and the ordering is not a preference. Today WriteBackRound.cs is half thread-safe: Join and Leave are Interlocked and HasFinished is a Volatile.Read - the parts written for concurrency - while Stage, TakeStaged, ReportRefresh, ReportForecast and TakeSummary mutate two plain Dictionary fields (connectionsById, stagedUpdates) and two plain reference fields (refreshSummary, forecastSummary) with no synchronisation at all. ADR-196 cites line numbers for these; the file has drifted a little since, so go by the member names. A Portfolio refresh and the Forecast it triggers already share one round (PortfolioUpdater:123 hands the intent over, RoundForNewWork sees the ambient round and Joins it), and the same happens when a refreshed team's data triggers a forecast from inside a Team execution. They are safe today only because one reader runs them one after the other. Introducing a second reader before the lock exists ships a data race on the path that writes fields back into a customer's work tracking system. So this is the precursor commit: it has no user-visible output of its own, which is why it is a commit inside slice 01 rather than a slice.

One private readonly lock object; every one of the five members is synchronous throughout, so nothing is awaited while it is held and there is no re-entrancy to reason about. Do not put a lock between Leave()'s atomic decrement and its own return value - WriteBackCollector.FlushAsync gates TakeStaged on that return value and it is the half that is already race-free.

Fold in the first of the two latent defects DESIGN found. UpdateServiceBase.WriteSummaryIfTheRoundIsOver gates on a HasFinished READ performed by EVERY execution in TriggerUpdate's finally, immediately after the flush already called Leave() (UpdateServiceBase.cs:127-140). With one reader only one execution is ever in that finally at a time; with lanes, the execution that decremented to one can read HasFinished after the other decremented to zero and BOTH call TakeSummary. The atomic take absorbs it - the second caller legitimately gets nothing. Do NOT change UpdateServiceBase: the fix belongs in the round, and threading Leave()'s return value through to the updater base would widen a seam for one caller. The property, not the lock, is what is asserted.

The stage-after-finish refusal is keyed on the staged set having been handed over, which is what the authored test drives (Stage, TakeStaged, then Stage -> throws) rather than on the execution counter reaching zero. Before committing, satisfy yourself that no production path stages after the take: WriteBackCollector.FlushAsync calls TakeStaged only when round.Leave() returned true, so the last execution out is the only taker. The QuietWriteBack and epic-5511-task-manager suites are the guard for that claim - run them, and if either reds it is telling you about a real late-stage path, not about a test to update.

The two structural checks are ADR-196's Earned Trust closing row and are DISTILL obligations 4 and 5. Obligation 4 is an ArchUnitNET dependency rule on the staging types (StagingKey, the two dictionaries' element types) - the repository's Architecture folder has a dozen examples of the fluent shape. Obligation 5 is a SOURCE scanner, not an ArchUnit rule: copy UpdateCancellationContextWriterArchUnitTest, which already does exactly this job for UpdateCancellationContext.Current. WriteBackRoundContext lives at Services/Implementation/WriteBackRoundContext.cs (NOT under .../BackgroundServices/Update/, despite what a reader expects) and its own doc comment already claims a single writer without anything guarding the claim; a second writer across lanes would be catastrophic rather than merely wrong.

House rules that will otherwise cost a CI cycle. Read docs/ci-learnings.md BEFORE writing code and pre-apply every rule it lists; the pre-commit ledger hook does NOT run in a git worktree - it resolves to the main checkout's empty index and passes vacuously - so grep the ledger's machine-readable patterns by hand over this step's diff. dotnet build must end with zero warnings (TreatWarningsAsErrors). The assembly declares [assembly: Parallelizable(ParallelScope.Fixtures)] and BackendTestParallelizationGuardTest fails the build on a new [NonParallelizable] without an allowlist entry - WriteBackRoundConcurrencyTest needs none, it constructs its own round and touches no shared host. Comments are rare and written for a stranger: never cite an internal document reference (no 'ADR-196', no 'DDD-10', no 'AC-01.5') as the explanation in a code comment - write the reason itself in plain language. The one exception is a #pragma warning disable, which carries its justification inline.

steps.name: Hold bookkeeping under one lock, and a displaced hold gives its round back
criteria: Mutating heldUpdates and scanning it for releases happen under one lock inside UpdateQueueService, so the serialisation the mechanism assumed is restored without restoring the single lane

A hold that displaces an earlier hold for the same key leaves the displaced hold's round before replacing it; the displaced round can still finish and everything staged in it still reaches the tracker
Two threads releasing holds concurrently against one satisfied hold release it exactly once - the callback runs once and the round is handed over once
ReleaseClearedHolds keeps its TryRemove-winner-only release and roundBeingHandedOver keeps its AsyncLocal; neither is changed
IsHeld still answers from the same dictionary and keeps its meaning for ForecastUpdater's guard
No lock is held across the released callback's database read; the winners are taken under the lock and released outside it
The existing UpdateQueueServiceTests suite stays green without being edited to accommodate the change
dotnet build zero warnings; the non-connector dotnet test filter green
steps.scenario_name: A hold that displaces an earlier hold for the same key leaves the displaced round; two lanes releasing one satisfied hold release it exactly once
steps.implementation_notes:
The second latent defect DESIGN found, and it lands BEFORE the lanes for the same reason 01-01 does: HoldUntilQueuedWorkClears / ReleaseClearedHolds were written against a single reader and are about to be reached from three. DISTILL scaffolded nothing here - these two tests are ADR-195's Earned Trust rows 'A displaced hold gives its round back' and 'Two lanes releasing holds concurrently release each hold once', and DELIVER writes them.

The defect, precisely. UpdateQueueService.cs:302 reads heldUpdates[heldFor] = new HeldUpdate(waitingOn, onQueuedWorkCleared, RoundForNewWork()). That is an indexer assignment: it overwrites last-write-wins, and RoundForNewWork() has ALREADY Joined the running round by the time the assignment happens. So a displaced entry is dropped without ever leaving its round, the round's executionsStillToFinish never reaches zero, the round never finishes, and everything staged in it is silently dropped - which is the exact failure the surrounding code's own comments (at :256-268 and :348-358) warn about. It is latent today only because ForecastUpdater guards with IsHeld first; it goes live the moment a Team execution and a Portfolio execution can reach that guard at once, which is what lanes make possible. Use the return of a TryGetValue / exchange under the lock and call round.Leave() on the displaced entry.

Two pieces of code here are ALREADY CORRECT and a crafter must not 'fix' them. ReleaseClearedHolds looks like a check-then-act, but only the TryRemove winner calls ReleaseIntoItsRound and TryRemove has exactly one winner - it is safe against double release as written. roundBeingHandedOver needs no change at all: it is an AsyncLocal, so each lane's reader flow carries its own value and the handover is a synchronous call chain within one flow. Both were recorded in DESIGN precisely because they are the first thing a reviewer flags and the answer is 'already correct' rather than 'fixed'.

One thing the design states that the code does not straightforwardly support, and it needs a decision rather than a copy. ADR-195 says the work under the lock is 'non-blocking and synchronous throughout'. That is true of the dictionary mutation and the scan, but ReleaseIntoItsRound invokes held.Release(), and the doc comment above ReleaseClearedHoldsWithoutFailingTheUpdate says that callback reads from the database. Holding one lock across a database read would serialise two lanes on it. Resolve it by scoping the lock to the dictionary operations: under the lock, collect the entries whose WaitingOn has cleared and TryRemove them - that is where the once-only property lives - then invoke ReleaseIntoItsRound on the winners outside the lock. C#'s lock is re-entrant on the same thread, so neither shape deadlocks even though Release() can call back into HoldUntilQueuedWorkClears; the choice is purely about how long the lock is held, and the shorter one is right.

The UpdateQueueService constructor is ALREADY AT 7 PARAMETERS. Sonar S107 caps it at 7, the ci-learnings ledger records a CI cycle lost to exactly this on a prior slice, and UpdateSubstrate exists because of it. This step should need no new collaborator at all - the lock is a private readonly field. If one turns out to be needed, group it into an existing parameter object or suppress narrowly with an inline justification; never a bare eighth parameter.

Fire-and-forget is everywhere on this path (_ = NotifyListeners(...), _ = TellListenersWithoutFailingTheCancel(...)) and the ledger records a real flake from asserting on a mock that a Task.Run calls without waiting. Any new assertion here must poll to a deadline rather than look immediately after a trigger. Read docs/ci-learnings.md first and grep its machine-readable patterns over this diff by hand - the pre-commit hook is vacuous in a worktree. Comments: plain-language reasons only, never an internal document reference.

steps.name: UpdateLane, the total UpdateType-to-lane mapping, and QueuedUpdate
criteria: UpdateLane has exactly three members - Team, Portfolio, Forecast
One total function maps UpdateType to UpdateLane, in one place; there is no second switch over UpdateType for lane purposes anywhere in the codebase
A test over Enum.GetValues<UpdateType>() asserts the mapping answers for every member, so a sixth update type fails the build rather than landing nowhere silently
TeamDelete maps to the Team lane and PortfolioDelete maps to the Portfolio lane, asserted directly for both members rather than inferred from the refresh mapping
Team maps to the Team lane, Features to the Portfolio lane and Forecasts to the Forecast lane
The mapping performs no I/O and reads nothing but the update type it is given - it takes an UpdateType and returns an UpdateLane, and depends on no repository, no DbContext and no connector
QueuedUpdate is a record of (UpdateKey Key, Func<Task> Run)
dotnet build zero warnings; the non-connector dotnet test filter green
steps.scenario_name: Every update type has a lane; a removal runs in the lane of the entity it removes
steps.implementation_notes:
This step carries DISTILL's obligations 1 and 2 - the two enforcement tests it could not write because the types they guard did not exist yet. DISTILL deliberately declined to scaffold the enum plus a total function purely to hold a test, calling it the one place a scaffold would have been real production code written by the wrong wave; it pinned D6's observable behaviour at the port instead (scenario 8, which 01-05 un-skips) and carried the exhaustiveness claim here.

UpdateType today has exactly five members, declared in this order: Team, Features, Forecasts, PortfolioDelete, TeamDelete. The lane table is Team lane = {Team, TeamDelete}, Portfolio lane = {Features, PortfolioDelete}, Forecast lane = {Forecasts}. Deletes share their entity type's lane because a delete running beside a refresh of the same entity type would be two things writing one entity at once, and because deletes are awaited by an HTTP caller already holding a response open.

Make totality structural, not just tested. Write the mapping as a C# switch EXPRESSION over the five members with no discard arm, so the compiler's exhaustiveness warning fires on a sixth member and TreatWarningsAsErrors turns it into a build failure. A `default:` or `_ =>` arm that returns the Team lane would make a sixth type land silently in the Team lane AND keep the enumeration test green forever - the test would assert that the mapping answers, which a default arm always does. The enumeration test is the second layer, not the only one: it must assert that every member gets an answer, and the two delete assertions are separate and explicit so D6's grouping is a pinned fact rather than a reading of a table.

QueuedUpdate closes S4 from the DISCUSS surface inventory: the reader's backstop catch currently logs 'Error processing update task' and names nothing (UpdateQueueService.cs:618), because a closure cannot be read by the code that catches around it. Carrying (UpdateKey, Func<Task>) does two jobs with one change - the backstop names what failed, and the lane is derivable from the item itself. It is consumed in 01-04.

Where the types live: alongside UpdateType.cs in Services/Implementation/BackgroundServices/Update/. Putting UpdateLane and the mapping in one file is fine and preferred - one total function, one place for D6's grouping to live, which is the whole reason it is not a switch at each of the three use sites (write, drain, read-model grouping).

House rules as in 01-01: read docs/ci-learnings.md before writing code and grep its machine-readable patterns over the diff by hand, because the pre-commit ledger hook resolves to the main checkout's empty index in a worktree and passes vacuously. Zero build warnings. No new [NonParallelizable]. Comments in plain language and never an internal document reference - a reader six months from now cannot resolve 'D6' or 'DDD-2', so write the reason instead.

steps.name: UpdateLanes - three channels, three readers, and a drain that covers all of them
criteria: UpdateLanes owns three unbounded channels and three reader tasks, one per lane; WriteTo(key, work) routes by the mapping from 01-03 and answers whether the write was accepted, and DrainAsync completes all three writers and awaits all three reader tasks together under the caller's token
The reader loop body carries over with its backstop catch, which now names the failing item's UpdateType and Id instead of logging 'Error processing update task' and naming nothing

UpdateQueueService no longer holds a channel or a reader loop; IUpdateQueueService's EnqueueUpdate and EnqueueAndAwaitAsync keep their signatures verbatim and the existing reflection freeze in ScalabilitySubstrateSeamArchUnitTest still passes, extended to cover DrainAsync
With a Portfolio refresh held open by a connector double that blocks until released, a Team refresh reaches InProgress while the Portfolio's is still InProgress
With a Portfolio refresh held open, a second Portfolio refresh stays Queued for the whole observation window
Cancelling the running Portfolio refresh through POST /api/latest/update/tasks/Features/{id}/cancel takes it to Cancelled and leaves the Team refresh beside it running
DrainAsync returns only once both occupied lanes have finished, and neither key is left admitted afterwards
A Portfolio refresh and the Forecast it triggers write exactly one round-summary line between them
An ArchUnitNET rule asserts UpdateLanes depends on no repository, no DbContext and no work-tracking connector - the lane is a queue concern and must not learn what it is running
Scenarios 1, 2, 5, 6 and 7 in Slice01TeamsKeepMovingScenarios.cs are un-skipped and green, stable over three consecutive runs
The epic-5511-task-manager and Architecture categories stay green; dotnet build zero warnings; the non-connector dotnet test filter green
steps.implementation_notes:
This is the step the reported complaint is answered by. It is a relocation, not a rewrite: the same Channel primitive, three instances, and the reader loop body carried over with its backstop. UpdateQueueService.cs:11 (the field), :602-621 (StartProcessingQueue) and the three queue.Writer.TryWrite call sites at :175, :220 and :522 are what moves; DrainAsync at :129-141 grows from one task to three.

THE CONSTRUCTOR IS ALREADY AT 7 PARAMETERS. Sonar S107 caps it at 7; the ci-learnings ledger records a CI cycle lost to exactly this on a prior slice and UpdateSubstrate exists because of it. Do not add an eighth. The cheapest honest answer is that UpdateQueueService constructs UpdateLanes itself - it owns the lifetime, it already owns processingTask, and UpdateLanes needs nothing but a logger and the mapping. If the lanes must be DI-registered for a test seam, group them into UpdateSubstrate rather than adding a parameter, or suppress S107 narrowly at the declaration with an inline plain-language justification. Never a bare eighth.

Things the existing code says that must survive the move. The reader loop takes NO update's token - it outlives any one update, so ReadAllAsync keeps CancellationToken.None; taking an update's token would mean cancelling one refresh stops the instance processing any others, and the comment at :604-609 says so. The backstop catch stays INSIDE each loop, so one lane failing cannot take the other two down - and with three reader tasks a lane can now die alone, which is precisely why it has to name the key. TryWrite failing still means the channel is closed, and AbandonUnqueuedWork (:247-254) must still run for that lane: it removes the key from the store, forgets the cancellation source and leaves the round, and without it the key stays marked as work in progress that nobody is doing. Dispose must complete the writers and not leak the three reader tasks.

DrainAsync: complete all three writers, then await Task.WhenAll of the three reader tasks under the caller's token, keeping the existing OperationCanceledException catch and its warning. It is bounded by the existing 30-second Shutdown:TimeoutSeconds. Scenario 7 asks for the drain while both lanes are held and only THEN releases the tracker, so a drain that returns early returns with the release still ahead of it - that is what makes the test able to fail.

Scenario 5 (the round reports once) would pass single-lane too, and it is placed here rather than with 01-01 deliberately: this is the step where a Portfolio execution and the Forecast it triggers can be in one round at the same time. Do not read a green at 01-01 as coverage of it. Note also that ADR-195 examined and rejected folding Forecasts into the Portfolio lane to avoid the concurrency: a forecast is ALSO triggered from inside a Team execution and joins the Team's round, so a round spans two lanes whatever the forecast's lane is. Merging them would buy no round safety and reintroduce head-of-line blocking.

The signature freeze lives at Architecture/ScalabilitySubstrateSeamArchUnitTest.cs and already freezes EnqueueUpdate (:9-12) and EnqueueAndAwaitAsync (:31-34) by reflection. Extend it to DrainAsync rather than writing a new file - IUpdateQueueService's caller contract is frozen by an existing test and stays frozen.

Flakiness, handled rather than hoped about. Fire-and-forget is everywhere on this path (_ = NotifyListeners(...), _ = TellListenersWithoutFailingTheCancel(...)) and the ledger records a real flake from asserting on a mock a Task.Run calls without waiting. Every assertion in the authored scenarios already waits rather than looks - positive claims poll to a 30 s deadline, negative claims hold a 2 s window open and watch it - so do not add an immediate assertion after a trigger and do not introduce Task.Delay-then-verify. The assembly declares [assembly: Parallelizable(ParallelScope.Fixtures)] and BackendTestParallelizationGuardTest fails the build on a new [NonParallelizable] fixture without an allowlist entry; none of these fixtures needs one, and if a scenario seems to, the scenario is racing something it should be polling for.

Deferred question 1 is already answered and needs no action: ThreeLaneSqliteWriteProbe runs green today and reports yes for safety, no for fairness - with three lanes saving as hard as they can nothing is refused and every save lands, but the incumbent re-takes the write lock while the others are in SQLite's backoff, so they do not interleave. That matters little because a refresh spends nearly all its wall-clock inside connector calls and nothing holds a write transaction across one. Do not add a write-serialising gate or per-lane save batching in response to it.

Read docs/ci-learnings.md before writing code and grep its machine-readable patterns over this diff by hand; the pre-commit ledger hook is vacuous in a worktree. Zero build warnings. Comments in plain language, never an internal document reference.

steps.name: A forecast waits for every refresh that feeds it, running as well as queued
criteria: IUpdateStatusStore gains exactly one member - bool HasActiveWork(IReadOnlyCollection<UpdateKey> keys) - answering the same predicate as the existing parameterless HasActiveWork (admitted and not yet terminal, i.e. Queued or InProgress) over the keys the caller names; HasQueuedWork keeps its name, its signature and its narrower meaning

Both adapters answer it identically: InProcessUpdateStatusStore in the keys.Any(TryGetValue ...) shape HasQueuedWork already uses, RedisUpdateStatusStore in the same single batched HashGet(StatusHashKey, fields) shape including its empty-keys guard
Neither Lua script is touched and RedisUpdateStatusScriptFreezeTest passes unedited - the new member is an ordinary read of the ordinal hash, exactly as HasQueuedWork already is

UpdateStatusStoreContainerTests gains a case in the shape of its existing HasQueuedWork one: across every combination of recorded states, the in-process store and a real Redis container give the same answer for the new member

ForecastUpdater's wait set is {every team of the portfolio} union {the portfolio's own Features key}, tested with the new scoped predicate, so a forecast waits for teams and for the Features refresh that fetches what it forecasts, whether those are queued or running
AForecastForThisPortfolioIsAlreadyOwed is unchanged - IsHeld or HasQueuedWork on the forecast key only. A forecast that is already RUNNING still does not make a later request stand down

The released-hold collision re-check waits for a forecast of the same portfolio that is running, not only one that is queued, so a hold released while a hand-triggered forecast is in flight re-holds instead of queuing a second run

UpdateQueueService's hold release asks the same question the hold was registered with - TakeHoldsWhoseWaitHasCleared uses the scoped HasActiveWork - and IUpdateQueueService.HoldUntilQueuedWorkClears is renamed HoldUntilNamedWorkClears at every call site
The UpdateQueueService constructor still takes 7 parameters

A hold naming a key that is InProgress is NOT released while that key runs, and IS released once that key's execution ends - both asserted, the negative one by holding an observation window open rather than by looking once
A hold registered from inside an execution that names that execution's own key is released when the execution ends, rather than waiting forever

A new acceptance scenario in Slice01TeamsKeepMovingScenarios.cs - A_portfolio_refresh_and_a_team_refresh_in_different_lanes_still_produce_one_forecast - drives both refreshes through the production queue with the tracker held open and asserts the portfolio was forecast exactly once

A source scanner at Tests/Architecture/ForecastTriggerCallSiteArchUnitTest.cs fails the build if any production file other than PortfolioUpdater.cs and TeamDataRefreshedForecastTriggerHandler.cs calls TriggerUpdate on an IForecastUpdater

ForecastUpdaterTest.Update_ShouldForecast_WhenTheTeamThatAskedForItIsStillRunningItsOwnRefresh is rewritten to state the new truth rather than deleted, and the two sibling tests that record a team as InProgress as scaffolding still say what they were written to say
Every TriggerImmediateUpdate_* test is green unedited - the button-press path takes none of this and must keep taking none of it
The whole of the DependencyAwareForecasting and QuietWriteBack categories is green WITHOUT any test in them being edited, including the two that are red today

TaskManagerAcceptanceTest.TheQueueGoesIdle waits for held work as well as active work, and requires idle to hold still rather than be read once - otherwise a teardown deletes the database while a forecast is still owed
01-04's five un-skipped scenarios stay green, stable over three consecutive runs; dotnet build zero warnings; the non-connector dotnet test filter green
steps.implementation_notes:
ADR-198 is this step's specification; read it before writing anything. This step exists because 01-04 reds two scenarios in a different epic - DependencyAwareForecasting/Slice00OneForecastPerBatchScenarios: A_portfolio_refresh_overlapping_a_team_refresh_settles_on_one_delivery_date and Refreshing_everything_announces_a_new_delivery_date_once_for_each_portfolio. Both fail because UpdateForecastsForPortfolio runs twice for one portfolio in one round and the simulation is unseeded, so the second run moves the date the first one just showed. Do NOT edit either test. They are the gate.

THE DEFECT IS NOT THE SECOND FORECAST. It is that the first forecast started before its inputs had settled. Forecast de-duplication rests on HasQueuedWork, which counts Queued only, and both IUpdateStatusStore.cs and ForecastUpdater.cs document that exclusion as deliberate. Under one lane a Team refresh and a Portfolio refresh could never run at once, so whichever asked second always found the forecast still Queued and stood down via AForecastForThisPortfolioIsAlreadyOwed. With a lane each, the Portfolio's ask finds the team InProgress rather than Queued, does not wait for it, and starts the forecast; the Team's ask then finds nothing to dedupe against and starts a second. Folding Forecasts into the Portfolio lane does not fix this and is already rejected - a forecast is also triggered from inside a Team execution, so a round spans lanes whatever the forecast's lane is.

THE FOUR CHANGES, in the order they are easiest to get right.

(1) The port. Add ONE member to IUpdateStatusStore: bool HasActiveWork(IReadOnlyCollection<UpdateKey> keys). It is an OVERLOAD of the existing parameterless HasActiveWork on purpose - the same predicate (Queued or InProgress), a narrower universe - rather than a third vocabulary word for the same idea. InProcess: keys.Any(key => updateStatuses.TryGetValue(key, out var status) && status.Status is UpdateProgress.Queued or UpdateProgress.InProgress). Redis: copy HasQueuedWork exactly, INCLUDING its keys.Count == 0 early return (Redis rejects a field-less HMGET outright and the existing comment says so), and widen only the value test. DO NOT touch either Lua script: ADR-182 froze MonotonicAdvanceScript and RequeueIfAdmittedScript, RedisUpdateStatusScriptFreezeTest compares them character for character, and like HasQueuedWork before it this member is an ordinary read of the ordinal hash. The container test copies the existing case's shape exactly - the QueuedLookups table at :26-32, the disagreement scan across both stores, and the CallsFor(commandStats, 'hmget') Is.EqualTo(1) assertion that proves the named keys are still read in ONE round trip however many teams a portfolio has. The discriminating row is 'only a key that has already started running', which answers false for HasQueuedWork and must answer true for the new member; without that row the two stores could agree on a blanket no and the test would prove nothing. HasQueuedWork keeps its name and signature - it still has a real caller and a real reason. Amend its doc comment to say where its Queued-only exclusion stops being sufficient, in plain language: the exclusion is right for 'is one already owed' and wrong for 'have the inputs settled', because work running in another lane can now be concurrent with the caller. Write the reason, never a document number.

(2) ForecastUpdater. The wait set becomes every team key of the portfolio PLUS new UpdateKey(UpdateType.Features, portfolioId), asked with the new scoped predicate - keep the existing coarse shape (one store call; if it answers true, return the whole candidate set) rather than filtering per key. Features_P is in the set for a correctness reason and the comment must say it: the Features refresh is what fetches the features being forecast, so a forecast that runs while it is mid-fetch is forecasting over a half-updated feature set. Rename the method to match what it now answers. The released-hold collision re-check (WorkTheWaitingForecastWouldCollideWith) takes the same set plus the forecast key when the forecast is ACTIVE rather than merely queued - a hold released while a hand-triggered forecast is in flight must re-hold, which under one lane could not arise because the running forecast occupied the only reader. LEAVE AForecastForThisPortfolioIsAlreadyOwed EXACTLY AS IT IS: IsHeld or HasQueuedWork on the forecast key. Widening it would make both red tests pass and quietly lose data - the team whose refresh triggered the later request would be reflected in no forecast at all until the next periodic refresh, up to three hours later on shipped defaults. The existing comment names that cost and is right about it.

(3) The hold. TakeHoldsWhoseWaitHasCleared must ask the SAME question the hold was registered with, or a hold registered against a running team releases while that team is still running - use the scoped HasActiveWork there too. Because 'clears' now means 'has left the queue' rather than 'has started', rename IUpdateQueueService.HoldUntilQueuedWorkClears to HoldUntilNamedWorkClears. It is NOT frozen - ScalabilitySubstrateSeamArchUnitTest freezes EnqueueUpdate, EnqueueAndAwaitAsync and DrainAsync only - and leaving Queued in the name would be a signature that contradicts the code. Call sites to rename: ForecastUpdater.HoldTheForecastUntil, UpdateQueueServiceTests (two test method names and three calls, around :872-:921), and Slice04StopARefreshSpecifications.cs:138. THE CONSTRUCTOR IS ALREADY AT 7 PARAMETERS and Sonar S107 caps it there; a prior slice lost a CI cycle to an eighth. This step needs no new collaborator at all.

(4) NOBODY EXCLUDES THEMSELVES, and this is the part to work through rather than copy. Both production callers ask from INSIDE an execution whose own key is in the wait set: PortfolioUpdater.cs:123 asks from Features_P, TeamDataRefreshedForecastTriggerHandler asks from Team_t. So every hold names its own asker. That is not a wait forever: RunUpdateAsync calls statusStore.Remove(:507) BEFORE ReleaseClearedHoldsWithoutFailingTheUpdate(:521), and RunAwaitableUpdateAsync does the same in its finally (:616 then :618), so a hold naming the asker releases the moment the asker's run ends. Do not add self-exclusion. It is what buys the guarantee: because every in-execution asker is a member of the set it waits on, no hold can have cleared while another asker is still asking, so the first asker holds and every later one finds IsHeld and stands down - one forecast per overlapping group, structurally, with no race to win. An ambient current-key context to exclude the asker would need a new AsyncLocal plus its own single-writer enforcement test AND would destroy that guarantee. Two ordering facts to keep straight while reasoning: HoldUntilNamedWorkClears calls ReleaseClearedHolds() immediately on registering, so a hold naming a key that is already gone releases at once (correct); and TryScheduleRerun's early return at :504 leaves the key admitted and Requeued without sweeping, which is also correct - the hold must keep waiting for the follow-up run.

WHAT THIS STEP DELIBERATELY REVERSES, so nobody 'fixes' the test back. ForecastUpdaterTest.Update_ShouldForecast_WhenTheTeamThatAskedForItIsStillRunningItsOwnRefresh (:326) pins the OLD behaviour and carries a comment explaining it. Rewrite it rather than delete it: the fact is still worth pinning, restated as 'a team that asks while still running is waited for, and the forecast runs exactly once its run ends' - which needs the real queue (CreateRealUpdateQueue, as Update_ShouldStillForecast_WhenTheLastTeamOfThePortfolioFailsToRefresh already does) rather than the mocked queue service, because a mock's HoldUntilNamedWorkClears does nothing and the forecast would simply never run. Two siblings record a team as InProgress as scaffolding rather than as their subject and will red for the same reason: Update_ShouldForecast_WhenTheQueuedWorkBelongsToTeamsThatDoNotWorkOnThePortfolio (:342) and Update_ShouldForecastBothPortfolios_WhenTheSameTeamWorksOnTwoOfThem (:360). Drive them through the real queue so the hold is actually released, and keep each saying what it was written to say. The two mocked HasQueuedWork setups at :280 and :298 move to the new member. Every TriggerImmediateUpdate_* test stays green unedited - that path bypasses all of this and must keep bypassing it; FeatureRankChangedForecastTriggerHandlerTest and FeatureOrderingPolicyChangedForecastTriggerHandlerTest both drive TriggerImmediateUpdate, so their HasQueuedWork setups are unused scaffolding and can stay.

WHERE THE PROMISE IS DEFENDED. 'One forecast per round per portfolio' is pinned today only by epic 5792's suite, which is not where the lanes are and which will not be looked at when the lanes are next changed. Add A_portfolio_refresh_and_a_team_refresh_in_different_lanes_still_produce_one_forecast to Slice01TeamsKeepMovingScenarios.cs, using the harness that file already has: hold the tracker open so the overlap is real rather than hoped for, release it, wait for the queue to settle, and assert the portfolio was forecast exactly once. Count it on a production seam rather than a double: ForecastUpdater writes one RefreshLog row of type Forecast per forecast execution, and the harness ALREADY reads the refresh history - UpdateQueueLanesAcceptanceTest.TheRefreshHistory() at :315, written for slice 02 and unused until now - so the assertion is 'exactly one row whose type is Forecast and whose entity is this portfolio'. That counts real executions, needs no new fake, and cannot be satisfied by a mock that was never called. Follow the file's existing discipline - positive claims poll to a deadline, negative claims hold a window open and watch it - and note that the epic-5792 harness's WaitUntilTheQueueStaysIdle already treats a held forecast as busy via IsHeld, which is the right shape to copy: a run that returns while a forecast is still owed does not fail this test, it fails the next one.

EXPECT A NEW LOG LINE IN THE SHUTDOWN SCENARIO, AND DO NOT CHASE IT. Shutting_down_waits_for_the_work_in_every_lane runs a portfolio refresh, which from this step onwards holds a forecast. The portfolio's terminal path sweeps during the drain, the hold releases, and the released forecast's WriteTo finds a closed lane - so AbandonUnqueuedWork runs and logs 'was not queued because the update queue is closing'. That is the designed path, not a leak: the key is removed, the cancellation source forgotten and the round left, which is exactly what AbandonUnqueuedWork exists for. The scenario's stillAdmitted assertion checks the portfolio and team keys, which are gone, and the teardown's wait for held work terminates because the hold did release.

ONE EXISTING SCENARIO STOPS BEING TRIVIAL, AND MUST NOT BE 'REPAIRED'. TaskManager/Slice04StopARefreshScenarios.A_cancelled_refresh_still_lets_go_of_the_work_held_behind_it registers its hold (GivenSomethingIsHeldBehind, Slice04StopARefreshSpecifications.cs:134-142) against a team that is already InProgress. Under the Queued-only predicate that hold was released IMMEDIATELY on registration, by the ReleaseClearedHolds() call inside HoldUntilNamedWorkClears - so the scenario was green before the cancel it is about had even happened. Its own comment says it waits 'on that key leaving the queue', which is what it will now actually do. It still passes, because the cancelled run's terminal path removes the key and then sweeps, and it finally tests what it claims. If it reds, that is telling you the release path is broken, not that the scenario needs accommodating.

ONE HARNESS FACT THAT WILL BITE, AND IT IS NOT IN THE NEW SCENARIO. TaskManagerAcceptanceTest.TheQueueGoesIdle (:220) waits on store.HasActiveWork() ALONE. A held forecast is not in the store - that is the point of a hold - so from 01-04b onwards the queue reads idle while a forecast is still owed, because every portfolio refresh now holds one where before it admitted one. UpdateQueueLanesAcceptanceTest's teardown (LetEveryGatedRefreshFinish, :58-63) calls it and then the host is disposed and the database deleted, so the released forecast runs against a dead host. That does not fail the test that caused it; it fails the NEXT one, recorded as though that test had asked for the forecast - which reads there as one portfolio forecast twice, the exact symptom this step exists to remove, in a place with no connection to its cause. The epic-5792 harness already met this and solved it: Slice00OneForecastPerBatchScenarios.WaitUntilTheQueueStaysIdle polls HasActiveWork() OR any portfolio's forecast key being IsHeld, and requires 25 consecutive idle readings rather than one, because there is a moment where a released forecast has left the holding pen and has not yet been admitted. Copy that shape into TheQueueGoesIdle itself rather than into the one new scenario - the base harness is where 'idle' is defined, eight epic-5511 suites inherit it, and the change only ever makes it wait longer, which is safe. Enumerate the forecast keys the way that harness does, from the portfolios in the database.

THE INVARIANT NEEDS AN ENFORCER. The guarantee above holds only while every coalesced caller is inside an execution whose key is in the wait set. Add Tests/Architecture/ForecastTriggerCallSiteArchUnitTest.cs as a SOURCE scanner in the shape of UpdateCancellationContextWriterArchUnitTest (same RepositoryRoot anchor, same obj-directory skip, same allowlist-of-relative-paths structure): the only production files that call TriggerUpdate on an IForecastUpdater are PortfolioUpdater.cs and TeamDataRefreshedForecastTriggerHandler.cs, and ForecastUpdater.cs itself is allowed because base.TriggerUpdate is the admission call. An ArchUnitNET dependency rule CANNOT express this - ForecastController and both rank handlers legitimately depend on IForecastUpdater for TriggerImmediateUpdate - so do not try to write one. The failure message must say what breaks, not which document says so: a third caller from a different kind of execution is not in the set the forecast waits on, so its request cannot be coalesced with the others and a second forecast moves a date the user was just shown.

TWO THINGS THAT ARE ALREADY CORRECT AND MUST NOT BE 'FIXED'. The round arithmetic: a hold joins the round in the enqueue's place (RoundForNewWork inside TakeOverTheHoldFor) and ReleaseIntoItsRound hands that place to the released work, so the round still finishes exactly once and still reaches the tracker once carrying both passes - Moving_the_forecast_into_its_own_execution_still_reaches_the_tracker_once and A_portfolio_and_the_forecast_it_triggers_still_report_their_round_once_between_them both stay green without change. And roundBeingHandedOver stays an AsyncLocal even though the release now regularly happens on a different lane's flow from the one that registered the hold: the handover is a synchronous call chain within the RELEASING flow, which is the only flow that matters.

HOUSE RULES. Read docs/ci-learnings.md BEFORE writing code and pre-apply every rule it lists; the pre-commit ledger hook does NOT run in a git worktree - it resolves to the main checkout's empty index and passes vacuously - so grep the ledger's machine-readable patterns by hand over this step's diff, unioning git diff --name-only with git status --porcelain so new files are not invisible to the filter. Run dotnet format analyzers Lighthouse.sln --severity info --verify-no-changes --no-restore before pushing: CA1859 in particular is armed by this step's shape, because a private helper returning an interface type where a List is built is exactly what it flags. dotnet build must end with zero warnings. No new [NonParallelizable] without an allowlist entry. Comments are rare and written for a stranger: never cite ADR-198, ADR-195, D6 or an AC number as the explanation in a code comment - a reader six months from now cannot resolve any of them, so write the reason itself. The one exception is a #pragma warning disable, which carries its justification inline.

NOT IN SCOPE, and each for a reason rather than by omission. AbandonUnqueuedWork still removes a key without sweeping for holds, so a hold naming work abandoned at shutdown never releases - pre-existing, shutdown-only, and harmless, because the process is going away, released work could not be enqueued into a closed lane anyway, and DrainAsync never waited for a held forecast. No filtering member on the store: nothing needs WHICH keys are still active, Count > 0 is the only question asked, and a boolean is one round trip where a filter invites a per-key one. And no change to UpdateController, AdmittedWorkOrdering, WriteBackRound, UpdateLanes or the lane mapping - this step is about when a forecast starts, not about which lane anything runs in.

steps.name: WaitingBehind names the holder of the asking row's own lane
criteria: UpdateController.GetTasks groups the admitted work by lane and resolves the holder per lane; a queued row's waitingBehind names the running row in its OWN lane
A queued row whose own lane is free has no waitingBehind at all - the property is absent or null, never an arbitrary running row from another lane
The resolution is a pure function of the admitted set it is given: 20 successive reads of the same state give the same answer every time, with no dependence on the order the store hands rows back
A queued TeamDelete stays Queued behind a running Team refresh and names that team, and never names the Portfolio running in another lane
UpdateTaskResponse keeps its shape, both routes keep their RbacGuard(SystemAdmin), and nothing is added to IUpdateStatusStore or either adapter
AdmittedWorkOrdering's comparator is unchanged; only its doc comment changes, narrowing its claim from the instance to a lane and pointing at WaitingBehind for the per-lane truth
Scenarios 3, 4 and 8 in Slice01TeamsKeepMovingScenarios.cs are un-skipped and green, stable over three consecutive runs
Slice02SeeWhatIsRunningSpecifications from epic-5511-task-manager stays green WITHOUT being edited
dotnet build zero warnings; the non-connector dotnet test filter green
steps.implementation_notes:
One line's meaning is corrected and nothing else moves. UpdateController.cs:61-62 currently reads admitted.FirstOrDefault(work => work.Status == InProgress) and calls that the lane holder, with a comment at :59-60 saying 'the queue runs one thing at a time, so whatever is running is what everything queued is waiting for'. That was true and stops being true at 01-04. Replace the single holder with a per-lane lookup built from the same admitted list - group by the 01-03 mapping applied to each row's UpdateType, take the InProgress row in each lane, and at :70 select the holder for the ASKING row's lane instead of the one global holder.

Keep it on the read path. Do NOT add a member to IUpdateStatusStore or either adapter: GetAdmittedWork() already returns everything (ADR-181), and putting a lane - a queue-implementation fact - into a port two adapters implement would be the wrong home for it. Do not add a constructor parameter either; the mapping is a static total function.

A green existing suite is not evidence here, and this is the trap. Slice02SeeWhatIsRunningSpecifications.ThenTheQueuedRowSaysItIsWaitingBehind queues one Team behind another Team. That is one lane under the OLD reading and one lane under the NEW one, so every assertion it makes passes unchanged whichever way WaitingBehind is resolved. The cross-lane case has never been covered by anything in this repository. Scenario 3 is the first test that can tell the two readings apart - and it reads the value 20 times over, because the old implementation picks it with FirstOrDefault out of a store several threads are writing to, and one correct read of an arbitrary answer says nothing about the next one. Scenario 4 is the second: a queued row whose own lane is free, which the old reading answers with the name of an unrelated running portfolio. If Slice02SeeWhatIsRunningSpecifications reds, that is a regression in the same-lane case, not a test to accommodate.

The absent case: scenario 4 accepts either a missing waitingBehind property or a JSON null. The current code already passes null for InProgress rows, so keeping null for 'this lane is free' is correct and needs no serializer change.

ElapsedOn, AdmittedWorkOrdering's comparator and the ordering of the response are untouched. The comparator still produces a correct, stable order - running first, then longest-waiting first, ties settled on type and id - and only its documented claim narrows: a queue position ACROSS lanes is not a number that exists, and the per-lane truth an operator needs is carried by WaitingBehind. That is a doc-comment change and nothing else; do not touch WhereItSitsInTheQueue.

The S6960 suppression already wrapping UpdateController stays as it is and keeps its existing justification. If a unit-level assertion is added to UpdateControllerTest.cs, it must construct the admitted set directly and assert the per-lane resolution as a pure function over it - that is the contract shape DESIGN assigns this code, and 'asserted over repeated reads' is the assertion mechanism it names.

Read docs/ci-learnings.md before writing code and grep its machine-readable patterns over this diff by hand; the pre-commit ledger hook is vacuous in a worktree. Zero build warnings. Comments in plain language, never an internal document reference.

steps.name: Close the slice - the sentence that stops being true, the full gate, and the live-connector proof
criteria: ActivitySection.tsx's comment above RowProgress no longer asserts that the queue runs a single piece of work at a time; it says what is true now - a mark per row, because several rows can be under way at once - in plain language, with no internal document reference in it. The component's production code is unchanged: rendering is already per row and correct as drawn

A TaskManagerIcon.test.tsx assertion shows two rows both reading Running each drawing their own progress indicator, and a queued row still drawing the waiting mark - so the claim the old comment made is now pinned by a test rather than by a sentence
pnpm test green; pnpm build completes with zero errors and zero warnings; Biome clean on ./src

dotnet build zero warnings; dotnet test green on --filter "TestCategory!=Integration&TestCategory!=JiraIntegration&TestCategory!=LinearIntegration&TestCategory!=AdoIntegration&TestCategory!=ServiceNowIntegration"; the story-5877-update-queue-lanes category reports 14 passed and 17 skipped (slice 02's), stable over three consecutive runs; the Architecture and epic-5511-task-manager categories green
The ledger's machine-readable patterns from docs/ci-learnings.md are grepped by hand over the whole slice diff, and any E2E test id touched is grepped across Lighthouse.EndToEndTests

AC-01.8 is answered by a live-connector test rather than a one-off observation, following the shape LinearDependencyDogfoodTest.cs already sets: a fixture carrying [Category("Integration")] and its own [Category("UpdateQueueLanesLive")], reading the connection's credential from an environment variable and throwing NotSupportedException when it is absent, so it never runs in the ordinary suite and never silently passes without one. It drives a Team refresh and a Portfolio refresh against a real Azure DevOps connection at the same time and asserts two RefreshLog rows whose [ExecutedAt - DurationMs, ExecutedAt] intervals overlap, one of each type. Azure DevOps rather than Linear, because the Linear key is shared with CI and repeated local runs rate-limit the next CI build; its token is AzureDevOpsLighthouseIntegrationTestToken, the variable the existing Azure DevOps fixtures already read
The new category is added to the non-connector exclusion filter everywhere that filter is written down, so an ordinary dotnet test run cannot reach the network through it

KPI-1's measurement is the assertion the live-connector test already makes, so what remains is a cadence rather than a mechanism: the delta records that the sample must be taken while both rows of a pair are still retained, against the instance's actual refresh interval rather than an assumed one. Taking the samples on a running instance is maintainer work and is named as such, not left to read as crafter work that was skipped

The answer to whether slice 02 is still worth building is written down - the slice's own learning hypothesis, answered rather than left open. This one needs the live test to have been run against a real connection, so it is the maintainer's call and the delta says so instead of recording an answer nobody produced
steps.scenario_name: Task manager activity - two rows under way at once each draw their own progress, and a waiting row still draws the waiting mark
steps.implementation_notes:
The frontend half of slice 01 is one comment. ActivitySection.tsx:88-95 explains the single spinner by asserting 'there is only ever one of those: the queue runs a single piece of work at a time'. That sentence stops being true at 01-04. The drawing itself is already correct - RowProgress switches per row on that row's own activity, so two running rows already draw two spinners - so this is a comment change and not a rendering change. Write the new comment for a stranger and in plain language: say that a spinner means that row is under way, that several can be at once, and that waiting gets a different mark so a reader can tell the two apart at a glance. Do not cite '#5877', 'ADR-195' or 'AC-01.1' as the explanation - a reader six months from now cannot resolve any of them.

The Vitest assertion is what stops this being a comment nobody checks. TaskManagerIcon.test.tsx is where the task-list rows are already exercised (DISCUSS's DoR named it as the frontend's test surface for this change); add a case with two InProgress rows and one Queued row and assert two progress indicators and one waiting mark, using the accessible names the component already sets. No new component, no new prop, no snapshot.

The backend gate. Run the non-connector filter exactly as written in the criteria - a bare dotnet test makes real API calls to Jira, Linear, Azure DevOps and ServiceNow and the connector tests throw rather than skip when a credential is missing, and the shared Linear key can rate-limit the next CI build. Known environmental failures that are NOT regressions, and which are not interchangeable: in a git worktree exactly 2 Licensing tests fail on the gitignored valid_not_expired_license.json (copy it from the main checkout); 10 failures in ReleaseServiceTest under load are contention and go green run alone; 8 failures in LighthouseReleaseServiceIntegrationTest are NOT contention and are excluded by the filter above; Octokit.RateLimitExceededException on GetAllReleases_* means repeated full runs exhausted the unauthenticated GitHub quota.

The ledger pass is not optional and is not satisfied by having read the file. Grep docs/ci-learnings.md's machine-readable patterns over the files this slice actually wrote - reading the ledger is not applying it - and remember the pre-commit hook does not run in a worktree: it resolves to the main checkout's empty index and passes vacuously, so every check here is by hand.

AC-01.8 became a test rather than an observation, decided 2026-09-18. DISTILL had recorded it as a dogfood check so that a green suite would never be mistaken for having covered it, and that reasoning still holds - doubles prove the lanes exist, only real connections prove they survive a real connector, a real database and a real write-back round. What changed is that this repo already has a shape for exactly that: LinearDependencyDogfoodTest.cs asserts against a real workspace, sits in an excluded category, and throws rather than skips when its credential is missing, so it can never pass by not running. Copy that shape. Azure DevOps is the target because the Linear key is shared with CI and repeated local runs rate-limit the next CI build. The test being repeatable is the point - it keeps being true, where an observation is true once and then is only a sentence in a document. Read the rows while they are still there: RefreshLogService.LogRefreshAsync trims on every write and keeps the newest RefreshLog:RetentionRuns rows PER (EntityId, Type), seeded at 30, which at the shipped 180-minute staleness threshold is roughly 3.75 days of history per entity and less for anyone who shortened the interval. The window is per entity, so a busy entity's history is shorter than a quiet one's, and the overlap test needs BOTH rows of a pair still retained at the moment it is read. That is why KPI-1 is sampled once a day during the window rather than read back as a retrospective afterwards - the fact is deleted before the proof is taken.

And then the question this whole slice exists to answer. Slice 01's learning hypothesis is that head-of-line blocking is the whole of 'hung'. If lanes are in and a Team refresh still stalls behind a held-open Portfolio refresh, the cause is elsewhere - the per-key execution lock, the SQLite write path, the connector's own HTTP connection limit - and that failure is worth more than the success, because the remaining candidates are all narrower. If it succeeds, slice 02 changes from a rescue to a tidy-up and may legitimately be dropped rather than deferred. Write the answer down; it is the input to slice 02's go/no-go and nothing downstream should have to re-derive it.
